evidence.quote: Most Dwarf words have several meanings.
evidence.claim: Selected senses must be stated explicitly and interpreted in context; do not invent additional meanings or morphology.
Every component is attested. Kol and Zan use colour senses, Bryn the shiny/brilliant sense, and Gorl the yellow sense; no metaphor is presented as another dictionary meaning.

evidence.quote: display colours and symbols from their clan and/or stronghold
evidence.claim: Military colour-and-symbol labels are culturally grounded. The source does not print the proposed compounds or grant these generated squads a canonical clan identity.
Reserve this attested clan label, rather than silently granting its history to a generated squad.

evidence.section: p.142, Ancestor Veneration / Honouring the Ancestors
evidence.claim: Reserve the printed Black Hammer clan name as well as Stonehammer. Naming a fresh squad after it would otherwise suggest an attested clan identity.

evidence.section: p.14, Chapter II: Skalf’s Hold, Cult of Gorlaz
evidence.quote: Gorlaz is simply another name for the Chaos God Slaanesh
evidence.claim: Exclude Gorlaz despite a superficially harmless colour-plus-axe decomposition.
Conservatively reserve Kolaz, a component of this canonical location; do not present it as an entirely new squad identity.

evidence.quote: Azul Metal of any kind; dependable; a sturdy Dwarf
evidence.claim: Select metal as an emblem material, not dependability as an earned personal quality. The same page attests Bar as a fortified gateway or door, and Drakk as dragon.

evidence.quote: Galaz Gold of particular ornamental value
evidence.claim: Ornamental gold is an attested emblem-material sense. Grungron on this page supplies forge imagery; neither word grants wealth, trade membership or ownership.
A craft-tool emblem is supported by an attested noun; it does not identify the squad as miners, masons or another military specialisation.

evidence.quote: Wutroth Wood from ancient mountain oak
evidence.claim: Retain the full material meaning in the gloss. Zharr on the same page means fire; fire-object compounds remain explicitly adapted symbolic imagery, not claims of magical gear or destructive deeds.

evidence.quote: Their symbol, the writhing Dragon with Grimnir’s seal, appears on their banners
evidence.claim: Dragon imagery occurs in Dwarf military heraldry. New colour/material dragon labels do not reproduce this clan identity, its seal, its genealogy or its military status.
Silver and bread are attested independent concepts, not invented product or wealth claims.
The glossary distinguishes a musical horn from horn material, and attests road and thunder. Selected nouns remain literal word senses inside adapted labels.
The selected moonlight sense and the printed material, shadow, work and sunrise nouns add distinct concepts. No generic machine, dawn-direction, geology or ancestry meaning is invented.

The conjunction explicitly pairs two reviewed images. Thrag means wound, Thrynaz includes laws, Tiwaz includes rest and Skaud includes song. These are not new translations for hospital, government or tavern.

High-resolution printed text confirms Zunthrum with n. Spear, money, sunset, remembering and gift are independently attested; none assigns actual stock, wealth, a historical event or a commemorated person.
